chapters.title: Chapter 5195: Eons of Advancements!
paragraphs: In THE Braneworld Observable Existence.
Another side of the same coin!
There was a grand chamber holding a particularly important personage.

The chamber was a vast expanse that defied the meager spatial comprehension of those born to the lower domains, its golden walls breathing with a rhythmic, luminescent light that suggested the structure itself possessed a predatory life of its own.
The surfaces were not quite solid, creating a landscape of crystallized purpose where every step resonated with power refined across spans predating THE First Cause.

Constellations drifted across the ceiling in complex, swirling patterns that held the weighted meaning of the emergence of THE Causes, depicting the birth of the foundational Causes that governed reality with a clarity that only THE Gilded were engineered to read!

A golden aquarium floated silently in one corner, filled with waters that shifted between deep blue and luminescent gold, containing a landscape of coral formations and underwater valleys that stretched for light years of compressed space despite appearing mere feet wide.

The floor beneath the floating golden lotus was a polished mirror of crystallized purpose.It was a room that served as both a throne and a laboratory, a sanctuary of the high-born under the whim of the Ubergulden line.

Now, THE Gesinde were gone, their golden-shining presence removed to leave Ubergulden Adelheid in a silence that was heavy. She sat upon her floating golden lotus, its petals radiating a warmth that sought to stabilize her foundations, yet the air around her was far from calm as she delved into the depths of her meditation.

Due to what Noah had done by flooding her existence with Infinity, potent rivers of multicolored Quintessence Infiniforce and shimmering gold Observable Force surged around her in violent, swirling currents that threatened to crack the very crystallized floor.
These rivers of power acted like predatory tides, clashing and merging in a display of existential weight that forced her to anchor her weavings with every ounce of her royal engineering.

The multicolored seas of Infiniforce pulsed with a rhythmic, tyrannical cadence that seemed to echo the heartbeat of THE Genesis Monarch himself, an intrusion of Bounded authority that was successfully masquerading as a Gilded bond!

The clashing of the gold and multicolored energies produced a low, thrumming sound that vibrated through the architecture of the room, causing the golden walls to pulse with a frantic, stuttering light as they struggled to process the anomalous frequency.

Ubergulden Adelheid remained a silhouette of regal stillness amidst this multicolored storm, her eyes closed as she fought to maintain the veil over her connection while the raw density of Noah’s infinity sought to announce its presence.
HUUM!
At such a time.
Ubergulden Dietrich entered the room with a heavy and measured tread, his golden eyes without pupils scanning the tempest of power surrounding his sister with a mixture of pride and mounting concern.

He took a seat upon a floating debris of crystallized purpose directly across from her, the weight of his own Paleozoic-tier existence providing a momentary stabilization to the roiling currents of the space as he sensed the sheer immensity of her shifting power.

He didn’t speak immediately, instead watching the way the multicolored rivers of infinity danced across her skin, his expression turning empathetic yet firm as he prepared to deliver the weight of their family’s expectations.
"Do you know why The Sororis Prima are making such a big deal of your Custodes, little sister?" Dietrich asked.

"Our family is powerful and we have significant pull even against THE Magna Sorora, but in your absence, something fundamental has changed while you were living among the dredges of the folds. Our Ubergulden lineage became even more distinguished because while you were gone in those eons, there was an incident and a profound advancement in our understanding of the enemy that blocks the path to the Source."
He leaned forward, the golden light of the walls reflecting in his empty eyes as he shared the secrets that the high houses guarded with their lives.

"After being blocked by THE Relictus for so long, we finally made some progress to understand them, and we believe we have finally found the path to... THE Primordial Source. THE Magna Sorora tried to enter a unique place where THE Relictus should be originating from, but none of their specialists survived the journey as all of one’s existence was stripped to their Source whenever any Gilded One tried to make the transition. The purest part of their existence and civilization was all that remained as no Gilded Ones survived the crossing, apart from those from the very few and very pure lineages capable of withstanding that specific pressure."
He gestured toward the swirling rivers of her aura, acknowledging the brilliance that infinity had amplified within her.

"Our Ubergulden lineage is among the few capable of surviving that journey, and your specific brilliance can shield one additional Custos, which would allow more of our forces to penetrate that place while gathering the information we need. We have become the spear that makes entry into the secrets of THE Primordial Source, and this is why the sisters care so much about the quality of the being bound to you. So tell me, little sister, who and where is your Custodes? Whatever the situation is, I can salvage it as long as it is not too obscene. Who and where...is your Custodes?"
Ubergulden Adelheid frowned, her internal thoughts moving with speed. She thought about her brother’s words and the staggering importance of her role in their family’s ascension.
Her eyes shone with a sharp, calculated light as she finally looked up, her voice carrying a cold and regal certainty that betrayed none of her visceral panic.

"They... are in THE Braneworld Observable Existence right now, operating under a veil I established to ensure their growth remained undisturbed by the politics of the houses. Let me take you to them in a little while, once I confirm something."
Ubergulden Dietrich let out a laugh that was filled with a free and resonant relief, the tension in his shoulders finally dissolving as he looked at his sister with genuine, dark amusement.

"Oh man, you really had me worried for a second there, for some reason I had the most ridiculous and impossible thought that you had somehow bonded with a Bounded lifeform as your Custos. An impossibility, I know, but existence is crazy like that and I find myself wondering what kind of wild tragedy that would have been!"
BOOM!

"And I did see you focusing on that group of Bounded Lifeforms when I found as I thought you may have formed a connection with them. Ah, I’ll check on that later. But can you imagine? If you had truly had a Bounded lifeform as your Custos while your position is so elevated among THE Gilded right now? Haha, what a wild thing that would have been to see!"
BOOM!

chapters.title: Chapter 5196: Entry Into THE Braneworld Observable Existence!
paragraphs: Any door can be opened. You simply need the right key.

The Bounded discovered this truth early. A locked granary becomes negotiable when you arrive with sufficient grain of your own. A fortified city becomes navigable when you arrive with sufficient gold. A suspicious guard becomes surprisingly flexible when you arrive with sufficient of whatever the suspicious guard specifically values, which is almost always money!
The Gilded Ones, who constructed THE Braneworld Observable Existence behind dimensional barriers requiring Paleozoic authority to breach, believed they had built a door without a key.
Because no Bounded Lifeform could reach Paleozoic!
But they had not built a door without a key.
The door, as all doors eventually do, would open.
It simply required the correct key.
And Noah had always been very good at finding keys!

Noah’s key this time was a Luxuria Gilded One he had put under his control as they were currently traversing endlessly chaotic seas of Infinity and Observable Force burning with Definition and Undefinition.

Custos Rani was already a Gilded One as her aura alone made this artificial barrier not act out against her, her glow covering both her and Noah as they crossed through. Even if she wasn’t here though, Noah still felt like he could brute force it, though that would draw unwanted attention that he wasn’t quite ready to manage.
Before he made the choice to leave the domain Rani had them in, he debated heading back down to THE Observable Existence to duke it out with Sororis Prima Prabhavati.

But the memories of Custos Rani allowed him to glimpse a bit more of her power as it seemed THE Magna Sorora were formidable, where even with his current means, even if Noah was confident, the battle would be loud.

In that all other THE Sororis Prima in THE Observable Existence currently would be alerted and he would lose more than make any gains, which led to the logical thought that he needed the power to one shot Paleozoic Scale entities in an instant to ensure everything would be smooth for the future.
But for now...
HUUM!

Existence shook and trembled as Noah felt himself passing through an imperceptible barrier and entering into somewhere filled with concentrations of terrifying brilliance as he found himself rising from a sea of concentrated golden Observable Force and emerging into skies of scintillating brilliance, intensity, and glory!
|We have made our entry into THE Braneworld Observable Existence. May there be boundless tyranny and Infinity in the future to come.|

His cells and atoms buzzed as they began to absorb everything nearby, and Pillow Talk activated as information began to flow into his mind even though he had memories to know exactly what he was looking at in the distance.
He had arrived in THE Braneworld Observable Existence, in a small corner of it that Custos Rani would have called her home!

Within THE Braneworld Observable Existence, nestled between the martial fortresses of THE Ira houses and the vast accumulation towers of THE Avaritia archives, lies a domain whose existence THE Superbius hierarchy considers simultaneously indispensable and somewhat beneath formal acknowledgment.
THE Velanthra.

Translated from the oldest Gilded dialects, the name means approximately "the place where wanting takes form," and the translation is considered accurate by every being who has ever entered its borders and emerged afterward with their existential priorities quietly rearranged.
Noah looked at the distant cluster of terrifying concentrations of power as he voiced out to Custos Rani.
"Which Luxuria Gilded One do you think would be ideal for me to collapse and take the identity of?"

He said such words casually as since he needed an identity, Noah didn’t want to go through anything bothersome as he simply thought of taking on the identity of a Luxuria Gilded One as he could easily emulate their Ego, in an even grander sense too!

And it would be a matching identity of a Custodes that Ubergulden Adelheid didn’t want others to know about. Custos Rani’s eyes flashed coldly, a sharp and clinical light reflecting in her galaxy-filled gaze as she processed the registries of her home domain.
"The Scion of Silken Grief," she whispered, the name carrying a weight of tragic isolation.

"He resides in the upper reaches of the tower, detached from the Houses of Service, and his absence from the social configurations of THE Velanthra would ensure your takeover remains undetected by the audit-eyes of the houses. He is also among thr possible identities I brought up to Sororis Prima Prabhavati."
Noah looked at the memories of the entity she mentioned as he smiled, a dangerous and dryly amused expression touching his crystalline features.
"Okay, let’s go see this place."

THE Velanthra spans a territory roughly equivalent to a small continent within THE Braneworld, its borders delineated not by walls or barriers but by a gradual transition in the ambient atmosphere that every visitor registers before they consciously understand what they are registering.

The air within THE Velanthra carries a density of amplified Luxuria Ego that accumulates across the first few miles of entry, a crimson-pink luminescence that threads through the observable light like a dye introduced into clear water, subtle at the borders and saturating at the center.

The architecture of THE Velanthra reflects an advanced civilization that has spent eons optimizing a single design principle: that every structure should produce in its observer the specific sensation of arriving somewhere they have always wanted to be without knowing they wanted it!

The buildings are tall and curving, their facades composed of a pale gold material that shifts its surface texture in response to the emotional state of whoever stands before it, producing different appearances for different observers as no two beings have ever reported seeing the same building in exactly the same configuration.

Rivers of Infinity flow through THE Velanthra in channels that were engineered during THE Sixth Age by THE Avaritia architects operating under Luxuria direction, the only known instance of a lower designation providing creative direction to a higher one!

sentences.text: Any door can be opened.
You simply need the right key.
The Bounded discovered this truth early.
A locked granary becomes negotiable when you arrive with sufficient grain of your own.
A fortified city becomes navigable when you arrive with sufficient gold.
A suspicious guard becomes surprisingly flexible when you arrive with sufficient of whatever the suspicious guard specifically values, which is almost always money!
The Gilded Ones, who constructed THE Braneworld Observable Existence behind dimensional barriers requiring Paleozoic authority to breach, believed they had built a door without a key.
Because no Bounded Lifeform could reach Paleozoic!
But they had not built a door without a key.
The door, as all doors eventually do, would open.
It simply required the correct key.
And Noah had always been very good at finding keys!

Noah’s key this time was a Luxuria Gilded One he had put under his control as they were currently traversing endlessly chaotic seas of Infinity and Observable Force burning with Definition and Undefinition.
Custos Rani was already a Gilded One as her aura alone made this artificial barrier not act out against her, her glow covering both her and Noah as they crossed through.
Even if she wasn’t here though, Noah still felt like he could brute force it, though that would draw unwanted attention that he wasn’t quite ready to manage.
Before he made the choice to leave the domain Rani had them in, he debated heading back down to THE Observable Existence to duke it out with Sororis Prima Prabhavati.

But the memories of Custos Rani allowed him to glimpse a bit more of her power as it seemed THE Magna Sorora were formidable, where even with his current means, even if Noah was confident, the battle would be loud.

In that all other THE Sororis Prima in THE Observable Existence currently would be alerted and he would lose more than make any gains, which led to the logical thought that he needed the power to one shot Paleozoic Scale entities in an instant to ensure everything would be smooth for the future.
But for now...
HUUM!

Existence shook and trembled as Noah felt himself passing through an imperceptible barrier and entering into somewhere filled with concentrations of terrifying brilliance as he found himself rising from a sea of concentrated golden Observable Force and emerging into skies of scintillating brilliance, intensity, and glory!
|We have made our entry into THE Braneworld Observable Existence.
May there be boundless tyranny and Infinity in the future to come.|

His cells and atoms buzzed as they began to absorb everything nearby, and Pillow Talk activated as information began to flow into his mind even though he had memories to know exactly what he was looking at in the distance.
He had arrived in THE Braneworld Observable Existence, in a small corner of it that Custos Rani would have called her home!

Within THE Braneworld Observable Existence, nestled between the martial fortresses of THE Ira houses and the vast accumulation towers of THE Avaritia archives, lies a domain whose existence THE Superbius hierarchy considers simultaneously indispensable and somewhat beneath formal acknowledgment.
THE Velanthra.

Translated from the oldest Gilded dialects, the name means approximately "the place where wanting takes form," and the translation is considered accurate by every being who has ever entered its borders and emerged afterward with their existential priorities quietly rearranged.
Noah looked at the distant cluster of terrifying concentrations of power as he voiced out to Custos Rani.
"Which Luxuria Gilded One do you think would be ideal for me to collapse and take the identity of?"

He said such words casually as since he needed an identity, Noah didn’t want to go through anything bothersome as he simply thought of taking on the identity of a Luxuria Gilded One as he could easily emulate their Ego, in an even grander sense too!
And it would be a matching identity of a Custodes that Ubergulden Adelheid didn’t want others to know about.
Custos Rani’s eyes flashed coldly, a sharp and clinical light reflecting in her galaxy-filled gaze as she processed the registries of her home domain.
"The Scion of Silken Grief," she whispered, the name carrying a weight of tragic isolation.

"He resides in the upper reaches of the tower, detached from the Houses of Service, and his absence from the social configurations of THE Velanthra would ensure your takeover remains undetected by the audit-eyes of the houses.
He is also among thr possible identities I brought up to Sororis Prima Prabhavati."
Noah looked at the memories of the entity she mentioned as he smiled, a dangerous and dryly amused expression touching his crystalline features.
"Okay, let’s go see this place."

THE Velanthra spans a territory roughly equivalent to a small continent within THE Braneworld, its borders delineated not by walls or barriers but by a gradual transition in the ambient atmosphere that every visitor registers before they consciously understand what they are registering.

The air within THE Velanthra carries a density of amplified Luxuria Ego that accumulates across the first few miles of entry, a crimson-pink luminescence that threads through the observable light like a dye introduced into clear water, subtle at the borders and saturating at the center.

The architecture of THE Velanthra reflects an advanced civilization that has spent eons optimizing a single design principle: that every structure should produce in its observer the specific sensation of arriving somewhere they have always wanted to be without knowing they wanted it!

The buildings are tall and curving, their facades composed of a pale gold material that shifts its surface texture in response to the emotional state of whoever stands before it, producing different appearances for different observers as no two beings have ever reported seeing the same building in exactly the same configuration.

chapters.title: Chapter 5197: The Custos, Osmont! I
paragraphs: The channels of this place wind through the domain’s central districts in patterns that follow the natural flow of amplified THE Desidero Cause energy rather than geographic logic, producing riverways that curve through plazas and beneath bridges and through the lower floors of inhabited structures.

The Infinity within these channels had been tinted crimson-pink through sustained exposure to the domain’s ambient Luxuria Ego, producing rivers that glow with warm rose-gold luminescence against the pale gold of the surrounding architecture.

Observable Force flows through THE Velanthra in an unusual configuration unique to this domain as rather than the ambient golden currents that characterize most of THE Braneworld, THE Velanthra’s Observable Force has been engineered into a mist that drifts through the streets at knee height.
Warm and faintly luminous, the mist responds to the presence of beings within it by producing gentle currents that press against them with the specific warmth of something alive and attentive!
Approximately three million Luxuria Gilded Ones inhabit THE Velanthra permanently, one of the largest concentration of any Gilded designation within some of the domain in THE Braneworld.
The Luxuria of THE Velanthra organize themselves into Houses of Service, each House specializing in a specific expression of the designation’s broad functional mandate.

Some Houses specialize in domestic refinement, producing the attendants who staff the grand households of THE Superbius rulers across the broader Braneworld, while others specialize in artistic production, generating the music, architecture, cuisine, and ceremonial design that give Gilded civilization its aesthetic character.

Others specialize in cultivation support, producing existences whose amplified THE Desidero Cause can accelerate the cultivation of higher-designation beings through directed emotional resonance and Dual Cultivation.

Since Noah had such terrifying waves of Luxuria, he pulled them back somewhat and covered his face with a crimson gold mask as they moved from the golden sea of Observable Force and into the periphery of THE Velanthra.

He could see groups of Luxuria lounged on crimson white sandy beaches, and some on the edge of the waters swimming while absorbing Observable Force into their foundations. In one area, Noah saw a group of THE Superbius and THE Ira Gilded Ones lounging on golden laid-back throne-like chairs, with an even larger ground of Luxuria Gilded Ones surrounding them as they fed them vibrant fruits filled with Observable Force.

Some Luxuria were filling their hands with pink and golden light as they gave massages to other Ira or Superbius Gilded Ones, providing a scene that felt like a domain of waste and debauchery to Noah’s pragmatic mind.
He shook his head and wanted to get past all this as his gaze shifted toward the towering spire at the heart of the continents-sized domain.
"Let’s go to THE Amaranthine Tower," he said, his voice flat and focused.
THE Amaranthine Tower.

From the memories of Custos Rani and what he could see in the far distance at the depths of this place, THE Amaranthine Tower was the tallest structure in THE Velanthra, a tower of pale gold and rose crystal that rises from the domain’s center and terminates in a crown of condensed Luxuria Ego visible from every point within the domain’s borders.
The tower serves as the administrative center of the domain’s Luxuria governance structures and as the residence of the highest-ranking Luxuria within the domain.
The entity for Noah to take the identity of was somewhere within that tower!

With a flash of brilliance, Custos Rani put her hand on him as she trembled from the contact alone, with Noah actually doing everything he could to stifle any part of his aura as it might pull in the hungry gazes of all Luxuria here.
Not yet.
Not yet!
Obtain an identity first, then conquest!
<The Scion of Silken Grief>

The private residence of THE Scion of Silken Grief was a masterclass in the kind of opulent cruelty that only THE Luxuria could engineer, the walls composed of shifting rose crystal that seemed to sigh with a faint, simulated pleasure whenever the light hit them at the right angle.
Dante reclined on a chaise of living coral that pulsed with a warm, golden light, his fingers tracing the rim of a chalice filled with the distilled essence of a Observable Force and Infinity.

A group of four Luxuria Gilded women, their iridescent skin marred by burns and dark, purplish fractures in their crystalline structures, huddled near the doorway as they tried to suppress their trembling.

They had been the playthings of the afternoon, their engineered foundations pushed to the point of structural failure just to satisfy the wandering whims of a man who had never known the weight of a single day’s labor.

"I told you to get out of my sight, you useless thingd," Dante said, his voice carrying the bored, high-pitched arrogance of a rich young master who found even the sight of his own victims to be a tedious inconvenience.
"You look like shit and your resonance is starting to give me a headache, so crawl back to your houses and try to look presentable before I call for you again later tonight."

The women scrambled out of the room without a single word of protest, their heads lowered as they retreated from the presence of a Scion who viewed their existence as nothing more than disposable fabric to be torn and discarded.

Dante watched them go with a sneer of absolute disdain, taking a slow sip of his essence as he settled deeper into the living coral, his mind already drifting toward which House of Service he would pillage next for his evening entertainment.
For he was ranked high among the Houses of Luxuria here and could do what he wanted!

He was just beginning to savor the silence when two distinct auras flashed into the center of his private domain, the sudden displacement of air causing the rose crystals on the walls to shriek in protest.
Dante blinked and looked toward the center of the room with an expression of sharp annoyance, his eyes narrowing as he felt the sheer audacity of an unannounced intrusion into his sanctuary.
"Fuck outa here, whoever you are,"he spat as he didn’t even bother to stand from his chaise.
"I don’t care if you’re from THE First of Service or if you’ve got a message from the Superbius houses, because I’m not in the mood for any more administrative bullshit today!"

The two figures didn’t move, and as Dante turned his head to fully address the intruders, his sneer faltered when he recognized the cold, galaxy-filled eyes of Custos Rani standing beside a man whose face was obscured by a crimson-gold mask.

He opened his mouth to deliver another insult, but the man slowly raised his hands and removed the mask, revealing a set of features that possessed a beauty so unfathomable and predatory it felt like a physical strike to Dante’s own Gilded senses.
HUUM!
The man didn’t say a word, but he released a fraction of his aura that caused the private domain to groan!

THE Scion of Silken Grief became frozen completely as a terrifying, absolute power locked onto his foundations, the sheer density of Noah’s Luxuria Ego flooding the room and turning the air into a thick, syrupy substance that Dante’s lungs couldn’t even process.
The rich young master tried to speak, but his voice was trapped behind a wall of Nearu Absolute Infinity that was currently rewriting the laws of the room to favor a new, tyrannical master.

He looked into Noah’s crystalline eyes and realized, with a visceral and animal terror, that he wasn’t looking at another Gilded One, but at a butcher who had finally come to claim the spoiled meat of his existence!
BOOM!

chapters.title: Chapter 5198: The Custos, Osmont! II
paragraphs: Noah walked forward with the unhurried gait of a man who already owned the room, his crystalline Luxuria form casting long, iridescent shadows against the rose crystal walls.

He looked at Dante, who was currently suspended in a state of absolute existential stasis, and he felt a flash of dry disdain for the way this fucking rat’s engineered foundations were trembling under the mere proximity of a superior Ego.

There was no struggle and no resistance as Noah reached out and sank his fingers into the air inches from Dante’s chest, pulling upon the multicolored seas of Quintessence Infiniforce to begin the systematic rewriting of the Scion’s existence.

He was gathering more and more information on Gilded Anatomy as soon, he would be able to engineer his own Hadean Weavings and those of his people a step further. Not merely going towaeds becoming moreso like Gilded Lifeforms...but something entirely new!

The multicolored light of Infinity dove deep into Dante’s Gilded marrow, acting as a terminal virus that tore through his memories of unearned opulence and replaced his autonomy with the cold, unyielding signature of THE Genesis Monarch.

Noah watched with a clinical eye as the rich young master’s internal systems were forcibly recalibrated to align with his own foundations, the pink-gold light of the Luxuria designation becoming stained with the heavy, multicolored hues of Noah’s sovereign will!
It was a brutal and efficient process that didn’t just bind the target, but essentially claimed the very concept of "Dante" as a piece of property to be utilized or discarded at a whim.
|Absolute Servitude of the Vessel integrated.|
|Target: Dante, THE Scion of Silken Grief, has been successfully rewritten as an extension of your Hadean existence.|
|Quintessence Infiniforce saturation: 100%.|

"You’ve lived a very loud and very useless life, Dante, so let’s see if your components can be put to better use in the dark," Noah murmured, his voice holding the resonance of a judge passing a final sentence.
He waved his hand with a casual flick of his wrist, and a lightless rift of obsidian energy tore open in the center of the opulence, revealing the cold and echoing reaches of THE Hadean Desmoterion.

Within this internal prison that existed in a pocket of his Organ of Civilization, the figure of Ozymandias stood waiting with his ancient and stoic bearing, his role as THE Warden being a position he performed with a silent, terrifying efficiency!

Noah tossed the rewritten and still-frozen body of Dante into the rift by kicking him into it, watching as the Scion vanished into the lightless depths where his spoiled existence would be archived, studied under temporally dilated condintions, and kept until needed, the rift closing an instant later with a sharp, metallic hum.
HUUM!

Noah stood alone in the center of the residence for a moment, and then he allowed his own crystalline beauty to shift and dissolve, his features blurring and resetting into the likeness of the man he had just displaced.
He looked at his reflection in the shifting rose crystal of the walls, noting the less handsome and more petulant features of THE Scion of Silken Grief with a shrug of his shoulders.
It was a significant downgrade in terms of aesthetic brilliance, but for the purposes of a disguise, he found the mediocre look of the rich young master to be entirely acceptable!

He closed his eyes and reached out through the Infinity and Observable Force that tied him to a certain royal, his consciousness traveling along the rivers of Observable Force that connected him to Ubergulden Adelheid.
"Hey," he said, his voice reaching her through the unreachable weavings with a calm and almost amused clarity.

"I found my identity as a Gilded One. I’ve taken the place of a boy named Dante, THE Scion of Silken Grief, who will be giving himself the additional distinction of THE Osmontian as of today. I’m in Velanthra right now...within THE Amaranthine Tower."
Noah opened his eyes and adjusted the silk of his new robes, a brilliant and tyrannical smile touching his borrowed lips.
She had mentioned she had hours at most before she had to give a name, and he was now here!

The pink-gold atmosphere of THE Velanthra was never meant to hold the weight of true, unadulterated sovereignty, for it was a place engineered for the softness of desire rather than the hard edges of command.
Yet at this time...

Above THE Amaranthine Tower, the shimmering skies began to seethe and tremble as a massive golden vessel tore through the fabric of the domain, its sheer mass displacing the rose-colored mists with a violent, authoritative pressure.

It was a leviathan of solidified Observable Force that burned with the searing, arrogant radiance of THE Superbius Gilded Ones, its hull stretching for kilometers like a floating continent of polished gold.
The ship didn’t merely fly but seemed to rewrite the gravity of the region, causing the rivers of rose-gold Infinity below to churn and overflow their engineered channels.
At the very center of the vessel’s prow, the logo of THE Ubergulden House blazed with a light that made the surrounding suns look like guttering candles.
It was a golden scepter piercing a lightless crown, with a singular, pupil-less eye weeping liquid starlight at the apex, a sigil that carried the weight of eons of unchallenged dominance!

Thousands of THE Luxuria Gilded Ones raised their eyes in shock, their pleasure-filled existences momentarily frozen by the arrival of a royal house that rarely deigned to step foot in the domain of service.
They wondered with a rising sense of dread why such an esteemed lineage would come to a place like this.
HUUM!
From the base of the massive vessel, the air rippled as three figures descended with a synchronized.
THE Sororis Prima...Evangelina, Konstanze, and Mathilde, floated down toward THE Amaranthine Tower, their golden robes trailing behind them like ribbons of liquid starlight.
Beside each of them walked their respective Custodes, massive Gilded warriors whose auras were so dense they seemed to bruise the very air of THE Velanthra.
These guardians moved with a clinical, preternatural stillness, their hands resting on the hilts of weapons that had unmade entire civilizations before THE Sixth Age was even a memory.
Behind this vanguard of authority, the figure of Ubergulden Dietrich appeared, his presence expanding to fill the void left by the ship’s arrival.
He stood with the easy confidence of a man who owned the sky he walked upon, his golden eyes without pupils fixed on the spire below with a gaze that held no room for negotiation.
Beside him stood Ubergulden Adelheid, her expression a mask of regal composure that hid the churning multicolored seas of infinity.
"Is this the place where your ’hidden’ Custos resides, sister?"
A pivotal moment came as many did not realize...it was the nexus point for change that would sweep across The Braneworld Observable Existence like a storm!

These guardians moved with a clinical, preternatural stillness, their hands resting on the hilts of weapons that had unmade entire civilizations before THE Sixth Age was even a memory.
Behind this vanguard of authority, the figure of Ubergulden Dietrich appeared, his presence expanding to fill the void left by the ship’s arrival.
He stood with the easy confidence of a man who owned the sky he walked upon, his golden eyes without pupils fixed on the spire below with a gaze that held no room for negotiation.
Beside him stood Ubergulden Adelheid, her expression a mask of regal composure that hid the churning multicolored seas of infinity.
"Is this the place where your ’hidden’ Custos resides, sister?"
A pivotal moment came as many did not realize...it was the nexus point for change that would sweep across The Braneworld Observable Existence like a storm!

chapters.title: Chapter 5199: The Custos, Osmont! III
paragraphs: Inside Dante’s domain, Noah stood amidst the shifting rose crystals and the pulsing coral furniture.

He calmly tapped his chest with a crystalline finger, and a ripple of multicolored light spilled from his form as another Nearu Absolute Clone emerged from his existence with the silent grace of a predator.

This body retained his true, unfathomable face and the staggering Luxuria Ego of Infinity, its aura vibrating with an iridescent density that made the surrounding air feel heavy and thick with the scent of ozone.

He beckoned toward Custos Rani with a subtle tilt of his head, and in the next moment, the two of them disappeared from the room in a flash of iridescent brilliance, leaving only his original body in the form of Dante.
HUUM!

They reappeared within the private reaches of Custos Rani’s own domain inside THE Amaranthine Tower, a space that was draped in fabrics of woven starlight and scented with the cloying, engineered sweetness of rose-gold incense.
Rani immediately dropped to her knees upon the polished golden floor as she felt the suffocating weight of Noah’s true presence filling her sanctuary.

She spoke with a voice that was hushed and trembling, her galaxy-filled eyes lowered in a gesture of profound submission that suggested she was struggling to anchor her own foundations against the radiance of her master.

"Master, this place is entirely insufficient to host the glory of your existence, for it is merely a small and meager corner of thid place that I have called my own across the eons. I feel the poverty of my own weavings when placed beneath the shadow of your Infinity, and I find myself ashamed that I cannot offer a sanctuary more worthy of you as we begin our work in THE Braneworld..."
Noah waved his hand dismissively, his crystalline eyes scanning the opulent fabrics and the rose-gold pillars with a dry, pragmatic disdain that made the air within the domain feel colder.

"Hush and stand up, the quality of your silk and the fragrance of your incense are of little consequence to me when I’ve already decided to treat this entire domain as the starting point of my conquest. Right now, this citadel of Luxuria Gilded Ones and these wretched, debauchery lands of THE Velanthra are filled with Paleozoic Scale Gilded Ones of all types who currently do not know me, but that’s a condition I intend to rectify over the next few days with a surgical and absolute efficiency..."
HUUM!
"I want to spread my influence through the Houses to bring this entire continent-sized place under my control."
He took a slow step forward, the multicolored rivers of his power pulsing in a rhythmic, tyrannical cadence that resonated through the tower’s crystalline foundations.

"I’ll take things lightly for now to ensure we don’t draw the immediate and unwanted attention of THE Magna Sorora, for I have no interest in fighting a loud and messy war before I’ve properly anchored my foundations in this place. These Gilded Ones and all their engineered pride and their eons of unearned glory shall be the first to truly understand their place in the hierarchy, for they’re going to witness the historic and absolute control of a Bounded lifeform stand over them!"
WAA!
His eyes shone with glory!
"We’ll have to be mindful of the most dangerous Paleozoic Scale monsters currently here but...the first thing that has really interested me is...THE Sanctum Velanthra."

Noah spent a long moment sorting through the fractured, iridescent memories of Custos Rani, finding that the most offensive disparity between his kind and these Gilded fuckers wasn’t just the raw density of their mana or the engineered perfection of their bodies.

It was the gatekeeping of knowledge, for while THE Bounded were left to scramble in the dirt for the scraps of an understanding they had to bleed for, THE Gilded had simply stolen the architectural blueprints of THE First Cause and called it their birthright.

Knowledge was the ultimate currency of power in THE Braneworld, and the specific hoard that interested Noah the most was a place nestled deep within the heart of this continent-sized domain of debauchery...a closely guarded sanctuary known as THE Sanctum Velanthra.
He closed his eyes in Custos Rani’s private domain and let the memories flow.
THE Sanctum Velanthra. It was a place holding information of...THE First Cause!

The sparse knowledge Custos Rani held regarding this place filtered through his consciousness with the patient clarity of information that had been kept deliberately vague from those below a certain standing, which told him immediately that whatever sat behind that name was something the Gilded considered genuinely worth protecting.
The first thing that landed in his mind was simple enough.
Bounded Lifeforms could not reach it.

Not as a matter of difficulty, not as a matter of climbing harder or cultivating longer or finding the right technique to bridge the gap. As a matter of categorical impossibility, structural and permanent, woven into the separation between the lower Observable Existence and THE Braneworld the same way the difference between water and fire was woven into their respective natures.

No Bounded Lifeform, regardless of what they had achieved or how exceptional their cultivation had proven, would find THE Sanctum Velanthra accessible without direct intervention from a Gilded One already present within it...which didn’t even matter since it was nearly impossible for Bounded Lifeforms to enter The Braneworld Observable Existence!
The Sanctum sat nested within THE Velanthra itself, which was already inaccessible to ordinary beings.
Three million Luxuria inhabited the broader domain and most of them would never cross into the Sanctum’s borders across the full span of their existences.

The border wasn’t marked by walls. It was marked by a shift in the quality of the surrounding existence so profound that beings who approached without sufficient standing found their own foundations pressing back against them, the space itself declining their entry without explanation or apology.
Several Superbius Gilded Ones across prior Ages had been turned back at the threshold.
That particular detail meant the Sanctum was not merely filtering for power. It was filtering for something else.
Entry required three simultaneous conditions, all established by THE Magna Sorora during the Sixth Age and maintained without amendment since!

chapters.title: Chapter 5200: The Custos, Osmont! IV
paragraphs: The first requirement was foundational standing. Ordovician Paleozoic at minimum. The second was designation standing, restricted among the Luxuria to those holding the rank of Prima Serva, and among all other designations requiring explicit Magna Sorora authorization.
Both of those conditions were administrative.
The third condition was the interesting one.

The entrant had to want to understand. Not to acquire, not to weaponize, not to accumulate. To understand. The Sanctum assessed this condition at its threshold through a mechanism no Gilded One had ever successfully mapped, and beings who arrived carrying motivations other than genuine comprehension were turned back with the same patient insistence as those who simply lacked the proper standing.
That was why the some Superbius Gilded Ones had been turned back.

Pride didn’t want to understand things. Pride wanted to possess things, to deploy things, to demonstrate things. The Dominion Cause that underpinned their engineering produced beings who approached knowledge the way they approached territory: as something to be claimed and administered. The Sanctum, apparently, did not respect that orientation.
Noah spent a moment considering what his own orientation toward the Sanctum actually was.

Genuine curiosity. Practical application, certainly, but genuine curiosity first and the application second. He wanted to understand what was inside because not understanding something that existed felt like a personal failure of attention. That seemed like it might satisfy the third condition, though he supposed he’d find out at the threshold.
Inside the Sanctum stood the Dreamstones.
Dreamstones that held...knowledge of The 9 Prime Causes that comprised THE First Cause!

Nine primary stones, natural crystalline growths that had emerged from the Sanctum’s ground during the earliest eons of THE Braneworld’s existence, predating every structure the Gilded had subsequently built around them.

Each stone had been shaped by the Prime Cause energy it contained rather than by any engineering methodology. The forms were organic expressions of foundational truth rather than designed artifacts, which made them the only things in THE Braneworld, from what Custos Rani’s sparse knowledge suggested, that the Gilded had not managed to put their engineering fingerprints on.
The Nine Prime Causes.
He turned each one over in his mind as the memories offered them to him.

THE Desidero Cause:existence wants. THE Dominion Cause: existence arranges hierarchies. THE Bellum Cause: existence fights. THE Cognitio Cause: existence learns. THE Vigilia Cause: existence is watched. THE Immutis Cause: existence endures. THE Consumptio Cause: existence converts. THE Mortis Cause: existence concludes.
And then the ninth.
THE Genesis Cause: existence emerges.

The only Prime Cause to which no Gilded designation had ever been connected, because the Gilded were born into their power rather than forging it through the painful emergence the Cause demanded as the price of genuine connection.

They had built their entire civilization atop an experiential gap where THE Genesis Cause should have been, and the gap had remained unfilled across all Seven Ages because filling it would have required them to suffer, and suffering was the one thing their engineering had been specifically designed to exempt them from.
But as of now...Noah knew very little about The Nine Prime Causes since he only had memories of Rani, and now Dante, to go off of!
A qualified being who placed their hand against a Dreamstone received, through the contact, not new information but foundational comprehension.

Understanding at the existential level rather than the cognitive level. The Pulses that could be derived from each Cause became accessible through that comprehension naturally, because Pulses were simply structured expressions of the Cause’s truth, and a being who understood the truth at the foundational level found the expressions available without the long cultivation process through which they were ordinarily developed.
Then came the part that made his eyes open without him deciding to open them.
THE Cause Incorporation.

The distinction between wielding a Cause and incorporating one was the distinction between borrowing an authority for a designated expression and becoming a being whose existence permanently embodied the Cause’s truth as a constituent element of what they were.

Beings who had incorporated a Prime Cause did not cast Pulses from that Cause. They expressed them, the way a being expressed their own Civilization rather than wielded it as a tool, the expressions available continuously, carrying the full weight of the Prime Cause itself.

Most who attempted Incorporation failed.Their existences were not sufficiently aligned with the foundational truth they sought to incorporate, their personal Civilizations too individually configured to subordinate themselves to the Cause’s broader axiom without fracturing under the pressure.
Very few had managed to incorporate even a portion of a single Prime Cause’s power. Those who succeeded shared one common characteristic:their Civilizational Access exceeded twenty-five percent.
Noah’s Civilizational Access currently edged an excess above 15%.
He had known this! The number had been a quiet background note in his cultivation planning, a threshold he intended to address once more immediate matters had concluded.
He thought about his Hadean Pillar of Infinity, which contained hundreds of actualized Civilizations, each one burning with the full weight of Infinity he had layered into it.

He thought about THE Absolute Forge of Infinity, where the density of Nearu Absolute Infinity had been compressed into every layer of his being. He thought about the specific shape of his own Cause, THE Infinite Cause, and how he had already been designing and planning to incorporate the power of his Cause into his Infinite Scales without ever having been told that such a thing was possible or what it was called.
He had arrived at the same destination independently.
He opened his eyes.
At this time.
Outside Custos Rani’s domain, outside the tower, he sensed Ubergulden Adelheid as she had come quick, and she was not alone.

There was a grand golden vessel of the Ubergulden House that blazed down fully and hung in THE Velanthra’s sky, its logo blazing, its delegation descending toward THE Amaranthine Tower where his disguised body was currently inhabiting Dante’s mediocre features!
He had a few things to manage in the next several hours.
But THE Sanctum Velanthra was very near the top of the list as he could observe Prime Causes and see if he could integrate them into his Infinite Scales alongside his Infinite Cause!
He intended to visit The Sanctum before anyone in this domain had fully processed what had arrived among them.

chapters.title: Chapter 5201: The Custos, Osmont! V
paragraphs: Noah watched from Custos Rani’s domain with patient attention.

Through the rose-crystal walls, the Ubergulden vessel dominated the sky above THE Velanthra like a continent that had decided to relocate upward, its polished gold hull displacing the crimson-pink mists with casual authority.

Below it, the three million Luxuria of the domain had collectively found reasons to be near windows, on terraces, at the edges of waterways, all of them oriented upward with the specific stillness of a population that had just realized the afternoon was going to be more interesting than anticipated.
He stretched his fingers, feeling the clone body he wore as Dante settle into its borrowed weight.
Time to go.

The Dante body emerged from THE Amaranthine Tower into the open air of THE Velanthra, floating upward through the rose-gold mist with the unhurried cadence of a being who had decided that appearing nervous would be the worst possible choice available to him.
Every Luxuria watching from below tracked his ascent.

He did not look at them. He looked upward, scanning the descending delegation. The three Sororis Primas, robed in layered gold, their Custodes flanking them with the dense stillness of weapons that had been set down rather than sheathed.

An Ubergulden Gilded One, golden-eyed and without pupils, his Observable Force drawing ambient currents to him naturally the way significant bodies drew everything nearby. And then, slightly behind him, Ubergulden Adelheid.
He smiled and waved!
It was a small wave! Several of the watching Luxuria below genuinely did not know how to process this!
Adelheid’s expression did not change.
The moment he appeared at the delegation’s level, the Sororis Primas assessed him simultaneously with the cold efficiency of institutions conducting a brief inspection.
Whatever they were looking for in the confirmation that he was genuinely Adelheid’s Custos, they apparently found it, because the displeasure that crossed their features was heavy!
They believed he was what he appeared to be.They simply found what he appeared to be disappointing.
Sororis Prima Evangelina did not introduce herself.
She raised her hand, and a blinding pillar of golden light dropped around him like a declaration rather than a question, and in the next instant he was elsewhere.
In the area, Custodes and all other Ubergulden also disappeared in a flash of golden light!
The skies above THE Velanthra held only the three Sororis Primas and the vessel.
Sororis Konstanze turned toward Evangelina with a flat expression.
"She really bound a Luxuria weakling as her Custos."

"Shall we kill him? It will hurt Adelheid’s weavings for the foreseeable future to lose a Custos, but she can then bond with an Ira or Superbius Gilded One who actually has power behind them after her existence heals. The current arrangement is an embarrassment to the Ubergulden name and a liability to the mission."
Mathilde said nothing, which was her way of agreeing.
Evangelina was quiet for a moment, looking at the space where the Dante-body had been.
"We are at a tipping point," she said finally.
Her voice came out cold and calm.

"Even among the Ubergulden lineage, very few have been confirmed to have the capability to survive entry into that place. We have confirmed Adelheid to be among the rare few, alongside her brother. That confirmation is not something we set aside because her Custos is a disappointment."
She turned toward the other two with the unhurried authority of a senior Sister who had decided where the conversation was going.

"Something can be weak, but we, THE Magna Sorora, are strong. The Superbius are strong. We have made Luxuria playthings powerful before, and we can do it again. We will make this one powerful enough to support Adelheid in that place. We have protocols. We have resources. We have Seven Ages of methodology for exactly this kind of problem."
Her mandala-eyes held steady.

"We have to seize this opportunity before THE Relictus find out and close it off. They will close it off the moment they detect the approach. They always do. Which means our window is notinfinite, and I have no interest in wasting it arguing over the aesthetics of Adelheid’s Custos arrangement."
She turned upward toward the vessel.
"Come on."

All three of them disappeared in the next instant. A nanosecond later, the entire vessel above THE Velanthra vanished alongside them, the massive structure of solidified Observable Force departing with the same casual authority with which it had arrived, leaving behind only the rippling disturbance in the rose-colored mists where its presence had been.
The weight pressing down across the domain dissolved.

Three million Luxuria breathed out in quiet collective relief, the specific exhalation of a population that had been holding itself very still in the presence of something significantly larger than itself and had just been granted permission to resume ordinary function.

The crimson-pink mists began to resettle into their usual drifting patterns. The engineered rivers of rose-gold Infinity returned to their channels. The beaches and the terraces and the waterways slowly repopulated with beings whose primary question was the same question every Luxuria in the domain was currently asking each other.
What had made it pertinent for the terrifying Ubergulden House to make a visit here?
Nobody had a satisfying answer.
In Custos Rani’s private domain, Noah’s other body stretched and breathed out slowly.
He looked toward Custos Rani.
"Let’s go see about these Prime Causes in THE Sanctum Velanthra."
He said it the way someone might suggest a walk, the tone of a being for whom the next item on the agenda was simply the next item on the agenda, regardless of what that item actually was.
Custos Rani’s galaxy-filled eyes blazed with fervor as she nodded and followed.
Noah’s mind was already sorting through the next several phases of his plans.

THE Sanctum Velanthra first. Soak up everything the Dreamstones held. The Prime Causes, the derived Causes, every layer of foundational knowledge the Gilded had spent seven ages hoarding on the upper face of the Observable while the Bounded below climbed through Vakochev’s limited framework without any of it.
Then the Royal Luxuria Houses within the domain.

He could not openly conquer just yet. THE Braneworld Observable Existence was populated with beings who could collapse him without breaking their focus, and advertising his presence before his foundations had grown sufficient was the kind of mistake that closed the game before the interesting parts arrived.
So he would not advertise.

He would do what a certain category of organism did when it found itself inside a system too large and too defended for direct assault: enter quietly, establish contact points, extend through the existing infrastructure along pathways that the infrastructure’s own immune responses were not calibrated to detect, and continue that extension until the moment when the system looked inward and found that the thing it had permitted to enter had already become a constituent part of how it functioned.
By then, removal would be complicated.
By then, removal would be so deeply entangled with the system’s own operational continuity that the attempt to remove him would damage the system attempting the removal more than it damaged him.
A virus did not announce its presence.

A virus did not challenge the body’s defenses directly, did not send formal declarations, did not register with the immune system as a hostile presence requiring immediate response. A virus simply found the pathways that were already open, moved through them, replicated along them, and waited with the patient confidence of something that had understood from the beginning that the game was not won through force but through proliferation, and that proliferation required only two things: access and time.
He had access.
He was working on the time!

Noah followed the rose-gold mist through the corridors of THE Amaranthine Tower with the unhurried gait of a being who already owned the building and had simply not yet informed the building of this fact.
THE Sanctum Velanthra was waiting!

He stretched his fingers, feeling the clone body he wore as Dante settle into its borrowed weight.

The Dante body emerged from THE Amaranthine Tower into the open air of THE Velanthra, floating upward through the rose-gold mist with the unhurried cadence of a being who had decided that appearing nervous would be the worst possible choice available to him.
Every Luxuria watching from below tracked his ascent.
He did not look at them.
He looked upward, scanning the descending delegation.
The three Sororis Primas, robed in layered gold, their Custodes flanking them with the dense stillness of weapons that had been set down rather than sheathed.
An Ubergulden Gilded One, golden-eyed and without pupils, his Observable Force drawing ambient currents to him naturally the way significant bodies drew everything nearby.
And then, slightly behind him, Ubergulden Adelheid.
He smiled and waved!
It was a small wave!
Several of the watching Luxuria below genuinely did not know how to process this!
Adelheid’s expression did not change.
The moment he appeared at the delegation’s level, the Sororis Primas assessed him simultaneously with the cold efficiency of institutions conducting a brief inspection.
Whatever they were looking for in the confirmation that he was genuinely Adelheid’s Custos, they apparently found it, because the displeasure that crossed their features was heavy!
They believed he was what he appeared to be.They simply found what he appeared to be disappointing.
Sororis Prima Evangelina did not introduce herself.
She raised her hand, and a blinding pillar of golden light dropped around him like a declaration rather than a question, and in the next instant he was elsewhere.
In the area, Custodes and all other Ubergulden also disappeared in a flash of golden light!
The skies above THE Velanthra held only the three Sororis Primas and the vessel.
Sororis Konstanze turned toward Evangelina with a flat expression.
"She really bound a Luxuria weakling as her Custos."
"Shall we kill him?
It will hurt Adelheid’s weavings for the foreseeable future to lose a Custos, but she can then bond with an Ira or Superbius Gilded One who actually has power behind them after her existence heals.
The current arrangement is an embarrassment to the Ubergulden name and a liability to the mission."
Mathilde said nothing, which was her way of agreeing.
Evangelina was quiet for a moment, looking at the space where the Dante-body had been.
"We are at a tipping point," she said finally.
Her voice came out cold and calm.
"Even among the Ubergulden lineage, very few have been confirmed to have the capability to survive entry into that place.
We have confirmed Adelheid to be among the rare few, alongside her brother.
That confirmation is not something we set aside because her Custos is a disappointment."
She turned toward the other two with the unhurried authority of a senior Sister who had decided where the conversation was going.
"Something can be weak, but we, THE Magna Sorora, are strong.
The Superbius are strong.
We have made Luxuria playthings powerful before, and we can do it again.
We will make this one powerful enough to support Adelheid in that place.
We have protocols.
We have resources.
We have Seven Ages of methodology for exactly this kind of problem."
Her mandala-eyes held steady.
"We have to seize this opportunity before THE Relictus find out and close it off.
They will close it off the moment they detect the approach.
They always do.
Which means our window is notinfinite, and I have no interest in wasting it arguing over the aesthetics of Adelheid’s Custos arrangement."
She turned upward toward the vessel.
"Come on."
All three of them disappeared in the next instant.

A nanosecond later, the entire vessel above THE Velanthra vanished alongside them, the massive structure of solidified Observable Force departing with the same casual authority with which it had arrived, leaving behind only the rippling disturbance in the rose-colored mists where its presence had been.
The weight pressing down across the domain dissolved.

Three million Luxuria breathed out in quiet collective relief, the specific exhalation of a population that had been holding itself very still in the presence of something significantly larger than itself and had just been granted permission to resume ordinary function.
The crimson-pink mists began to resettle into their usual drifting patterns.
The engineered rivers of rose-gold Infinity returned to their channels.
The beaches and the terraces and the waterways slowly repopulated with beings whose primary question was the same question every Luxuria in the domain was currently asking each other.
What had made it pertinent for the terrifying Ubergulden House to make a visit here?
Nobody had a satisfying answer.
In Custos Rani’s private domain, Noah’s other body stretched and breathed out slowly.
He looked toward Custos Rani.
"Let’s go see about these Prime Causes in THE Sanctum Velanthra."
He said it the way someone might suggest a walk, the tone of a being for whom the next item on the agenda was simply the next item on the agenda, regardless of what that item actually was.
Custos Rani’s galaxy-filled eyes blazed with fervor as she nodded and followed.
Noah’s mind was already sorting through the next several phases of his plans.
THE Sanctum Velanthra first.
Soak up everything the Dreamstones held.

The Prime Causes, the derived Causes, every layer of foundational knowledge the Gilded had spent seven ages hoarding on the upper face of the Observable while the Bounded below climbed through Vakochev’s limited framework without any of it.
Then the Royal Luxuria Houses within the domain.
He could not openly conquer just yet.

THE Braneworld Observable Existence was populated with beings who could collapse him without breaking their focus, and advertising his presence before his foundations had grown sufficient was the kind of mistake that closed the game before the interesting parts arrived.
So he would not advertise.

He would do what a certain category of organism did when it found itself inside a system too large and too defended for direct assault: enter quietly, establish contact points, extend through the existing infrastructure along pathways that the infrastructure’s own immune responses were not calibrated to detect, and continue that extension until the moment when the system looked inward and found that the thing it had permitted to enter had already become a constituent part of how it functioned.
By then, removal would be complicated.
By then, removal would be so deeply entangled with the system’s own operational continuity that the attempt to remove him would damage the system attempting the removal more than it damaged him.
A virus did not announce its presence.
A virus did not challenge the body’s defenses directly, did not send formal declarations, did not register with the immune system as a hostile presence requiring immediate response.

A virus simply found the pathways that were already open, moved through them, replicated along them, and waited with the patient confidence of something that had understood from the beginning that the game was not won through force but through proliferation, and that proliferation required only two things: access and time.
He had access.
He was working on the time!

Noah followed the rose-gold mist through the corridors of THE Amaranthine Tower with the unhurried gait of a being who already owned the building and had simply not yet informed the building of this fact.
THE Sanctum Velanthra was waiting!

chapters.title: Chapter 5202: The Custos, Osmont! VI
paragraphs: The interior of the Ubergulden vessel was minimal in the way that genuine power tends to be minimal, stripped of the decorative excess that lesser houses used to communicate their standing because the Ubergulden standing did not require communication.
The walls were pale gold, smooth and unadorned. The floor carried the same quality. The air held a density of concentrated Observable Force.
Noah looked around once.
Space flickered gold ahead of him.

Ubergulden Adelheid materialized first, and before her stood a Gilded One whose presence arrived before his features did, the Observable Force in the room bending toward him with the natural deference of currents acknowledging a significant body. Fair skin, white robes, golden eyes with no pupils.
The Gilded One looked at him with a dangerous smile that carried more edge than warmth, his pupilless eyes moving across Noah’s borrowed Dante features.
"My sister truly bonded with a weak Luxuria?"
The voice held the pleasant cadence of someone asking a question they already found offensive.
"How did this come about? You." His gaze sharpened. "How did this come about?"
Noah’s eyes were bright.
This was the brother of Ubergulden Adelheid, then!
Infinity buzzer as information flowed.
Ubergulden Dietrich. In the flesh!
Adelheid’s voice arrived through their connection a half-breath before he needed it.
’Keep it light and simple. We met in Velanthra a long time ago. I enjoyed your company and a bond inadvertently formed.’
She moved from behind her brother as she said it, her expression the composed neutrality of a being navigating a conversation with extremely limited margin for error.
Noah smiled at Dietrich.
"We met in Velanthra a long time ago," he said pleasantly. "After she spent a few nights with me..."
BOOM!

Dietrich moved at a speed that bypassed the ordinary interval between decision and action, his hand closing around Noah’s neck and driving him backward into the vessel wall with a force that left the pale gold surface groaning around the point of impact.
The impact registered through the Dante body without the existential disruption it would have produced in an ordinary Luxuria!
Dietrich’s eyes had gone cold.
"You good for nothing pleasure sack."
His voice came out low and even, which was somehow more alarming than if it had come out loud.
"Do you even know where you find yourself? The weavings you are now connected to? Do not fuck around when you are talking to me."His grip tightened fractionally.
"If I ask you to detail events, you detail them while gazing down and not even meeting my eyes. If I ask you to kneel, you kneel. Now."
His free hand began to shine.

"I ask you, do you have any negative intentions toward the Ubergulden House? Is there any trickery occurring that I need to know about? Answer clearly. Otherwise your existence will end here, however much damage this will do."

The power blooming from his shining hand was not the Observable Force that had been rushing to him since his arrival. It was something older and more fundamental, drawing from a well beneath the ordinary substrates of Gilded cultivation!
|Warning: Entity ahead is drawing from THE Mortis Cause directly.|

|The power of ending itself is being channeled as a truth-enforcement mechanism. Should any falsehood stem from your existence while this power is active, the Cause will sense the discrepancy between what is stated and what is real and seek to collapse the causality of the statement’s source.|
|This is not a technique or a Pulse. This is Prime Cause authority.|
Noah looked into Ubergulden Dietrich’s pupilless golden eyes.

The Mortis Cause. The foundational truth that existence concludes, wielded directly rather than through derived technique, applied to him as a lie detector by a being who clearly did not consider him significant enough!
Burning defiance rose within him!
"Get," he said, his voice carrying the cold flat cadence of a final instruction, "your fucking hands off of me."
BOOM!
Dietrich blinked.
His grip tightened rather than releasing, his head tilting with the bemused expression of a being encountering something that did not fit the expected parameters of the current situation.
A Luxuria dared to speak to Superbius Gilded One this way?
He leaned forward slightly, bringing his face closer to Noah’s borrowed features with an expression that held genuine incredulity beneath its cold surface.
"Your Engineering shouldnt even make defiance possible. My sister’s Custos, a Luxuria Lifeform, is truly being defiant against me right now?"
He almost sounded delighted by this. Almost.
Ubergulden Adelheid moved between them.
Her gaze was chilly!
"Let him go."
WAA!
Her body buzzed with Quintessence Infiniforce as she said it, the multicolored currents surging outward from her foundations in a way that was not aggressive but was also not a request.
The Infiniforce that had been flooding into her from Noah’s bond for all the time they had been connected surged with the specific responsiveness of substance being called upon.
And at such a time Noah felt something shift inside him!
|Unknown resonance between the established connection between you and Ubergulden Adelheid is activating.|

|The workings and weavings of Custodes attached to Gilded Ones are being fully integrated into your existence. Your Infinite Cause senses boundless potential and challenges ahead and is reforming this connection into something previously unknown.|

|The boundless Infinity you have flooded into Ubergulden Adelheid can allow a semblance of her power to be borrowed from her when she is in close proximity. New capability established:Infinite Existential Empowerment.|
|The connection between you, a Hadean Lifeform, and Ubergulden Adelheid, a Gilded Lifeform, is the first of its kind across the recorded history. Refinement is ongoing.|
HUUM!

Ubergulden Adelheid’s body was filled with power. His own body was filled with power. The Infinity he had poured into her across the duration of their bond connected to herPaleozoic Scale and now existed within reach, available to be drawn upon through the proximity that activated the resonance, and he pulled from it without deliberating over whether to pull!
BOOM!

A terrifying concentration of Infinity and Observable Force gushed from him and shrouded his figure in multicolored flames that had no business appearing on a Luxuria Gilded One in any framework the Gilded had ever developed.
His Pillar of Infinity buzzed while being invisible! His Hadean Bones and Organs roared as Nearu Absolute Infinity demanded for him to not be held by the neck!
HUUM!

The hand of Ubergulden Dietrich buzzed violently against his neck as the force pressed outward from his foundations and forced the grip to release, the Gilded One’s fingers separating from his throat under pressure that clearly exceeded what Dietrich had calculated the Dante-body capable of producing.
Dietrich stepped back!
His pupilless eyes moved between Noah and his sister with a new expression, the dangerous smile gone, the cold assessment replaced by something that held more actual attention.

Between Noah and Ubergulden Adelheid, a surging river of Infinity buzzed with visible luminescence, the connection between them no longer subtle but undeniably present, a bond between a Hadean Lifeform wearing a Luxuria skin and a Gilded One!
The door of the vessel’s interior opened.

The three Sororis Primas entered, and Sororis Prima Evangelina’s eyes sharpened the moment they registered what they were looking at. Her mandala-eyes rotated through several configurations with the rapid adjustment.
"A profound resonance between a Custodes and their Ingenue."
Her eyes did not leave the luminous river connecting Noah to Adelheid.
"A resonance rarely achieved by any bonded pair..."

chapters.title: Chapter 5203: A Terrifying Advancement!
paragraphs: Something had shifted in how the air felt.

Since arriving in THE Braneworld Observable Existence, Noah had been aware of a subtle resistance in the ambient Infinity here, the specific quality of a medium that had not been calibrated for his kind of power. Not debilitating. Just present. A constant low-level friction between what he was and what this place expected its inhabitants to be.
The Infinite Existential Empowerment dissolved that friction entirely.

The surging river of connection between him and Ubergulden Adelheid blazed with visible luminescence, and through that river the Infinity of THE Braneworld stopped resisting him and started flowing toward him the way it flowed toward beings who belonged here.

He breathed easier. He perceived farther. The flows of information that Infinity touched in the surrounding space began returning feedback to him with the generosity of a medium that had just decided to cooperate.

Pillow Talk was already working. The passive capability of his Absolute Luxuria Ego had been pulling ambient information since he arrived, but with the resistance gone it operated at a different level entirely. The weavings of information in the surrounding space were not merely available...they were streaming toward him as if existence itself had decided that his current objectives merited its full disclosure.
The secrets, the knowledge, the carefully hoarded truths of this elevated domain.
They simply flowed.
|Existence speaks:|

|The three beings designated Sororis Prima carry engineering that exceeds standard Ordovician Paleozoic classification. Silurian Paleozoic proximity confirmed for all three. Their foundations are actively pulling from THE Cognitio Cause, the Prime Cause governing knowledge and comprehension. They do not merely wield derived Civilizations anchored in learning. They have incorporated partial Cognitio Cause authority into their existences.|
|Sororis Prima Evangelina: Civilizational Access: approximately 31%. The highest of the three.|
|Sororis Prima Konstanze: Civilizational Access: approximately 27%.|
|Sororis Prima Mathilde: Civilizational Access: approximately 25%.|
|All three exceed the 25% threshold required for Prime Cause Incorporation attempts. All three have succeeded where most Gilded Ones fail.|

|Additional observation: The vessel you currently occupy is a sovereign domain of the Ubergulden House, registered as exempt from standard Magna Sorora surveillance protocols. Conversations within it carry no external record...|
Noah’s eyes were bright as he processed all of it and focused on Evangelina.
The most capable of the three. Thirty-one percent Civilizational Access!
Evangelina looked at him directly as she spoke, though her words covered the room.

"The connection between a Gilded One and their Custodes is unique. After they have been with one another for eons, they develop such a strong sense of trust that their existences can resonate to form an even grander bond, allowing power to be shared between the two seamlessly while both are empowered from it."
Her mandala-eyes rotated slowly.
"A Primaris Bond. Even I do not have such a bond with my own Custodes." A brief pause that carried neither self-pity nor complaint, only assessment.
"I was worried about a weak, lust-filled Gilded One being your Custodes. But it seems that even still, you are not entirely without instinct. This arrangement works for now."
Her gaze shifted.
"Dietrich. You and your sister need to get ready."
Dietrich’s frown arrived immediately, his pupilless golden eyes moving from Evangelina to Noah.
"We still need to understand everything about him. What he has been doing these past eons, what his intentions are, how this bond actually formed-"
"We have already taken care of all of it."
Evangelina’s voice did not rise. It simply closed the subject.

"Need I remind you that we do not have time? If we lose this opportunity, THE Relictus will find out about our advancements and everything will be closed off once more. Every delay is a door shutting."
Noah’s eyes shone at the mention of THE Relictus as he thought of someone.

THE Creature. Was he still running? Had he managed to escape the Gilded pursuit, or had THE Gilded Ones closed the distance? He turned the question over briefly and filed it, because the more immediate thread was the one Evangelina kept pulling toward.
An opportunity that THE Relictus would close off if they detected the advancement.

He had not looked at Ubergulden Adelheid as a source of access to anything this significant. She had been a battery. A connection. A bridge into the Braneworld. Useful, genuinely useful, but useful in the way that a key was useful: for getting through a door rather than for what the door contained.
It seemed there was considerably more door than he had calculated.

He did not turn around. He kept his gaze forward on Evangelina and spoke quietly through the river of connection that continued to buzz between him and Adelheid, his voice arriving in her consciousness through the same channels her Observable Force arrived in his.
’It seems there were a lot of things you didn’t tell me. I would have acclimated much better and done things considerably faster.’

He felt her attention shift toward the visible river between them. He was keeping it active deliberately because the Infinite Existential Empowerment required her proximity and and he had no interest in Dietrich’s hand finding his throat again.
Her reply came calm and measured through the connection.

’I have also been gone for a long time. I only know a little more than you do. But this is not something you should look at as an opportunity. Multiple Gilded Ones have already died from this. Ones with far more preparation and far more power than you currently possess. You are not even a Gilded One. Envision what might happen to you if the same thing that killed them happens to you.’
She was trying to scare him off.
It was having the opposite effect!
He kept his expression neutral as Evangelina’s voice rolled out again, stronger now.

"For countless eons beyond counting, THE Primordial Source has remained outside our grasp. But we have made tremendous advancements in recent times."Her mandala-eyes held both him and Adelheid in their rotating geometry.

"Some unique Royal Gilded Ones are capable of accessing a place that cannot be entered with ordinary weavings of Existence. Your body, your power, your Civilization... to enter that place, much of this is left behind. Purified. Only your Soul, surrounded by your Ego and your Observable Force and your Infinity, makes it through. We believe it is because of the boundless purity of THE Primordial Source in that place. The more we are able to send there, the more that survive, the more we can grasp its secrets."
She held steady.

"You, and other Royal Gilded Ones and their Custodes, will be sent in the next round. This is a race to access THE Primordial Source before THE Relictus detect our advancements and close the approach once more. But it is also a race against every other Royal House of the Gilded."
Something shifted behind her clinical composure!
"I am a Sororis Prima of THE Magna Sorora. But I have never forgotten that I am Ubergulden. Our lineage cannot fall behind."
